newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance firms' Q3 not as bad as expected.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance firms' Q3 not as bad as expected.

text.p: Third-quarter results from major Thai finance and securities companies released on Monday were poor but not as bad as most investors had expected, analysts said.

"Generally the results weren't so great," said Jennifer Gandin, finance and securities analyst at the Multi Credit Corporation of Thailand. "But the market has responded positively which makes me think much of the bad news has been discounted."
Finance shares have been mauled since the start of October with institutional sales and worries about loan quality sparking a 25.6 percent sell off in the sector.

Among gainers into the afternoon session were Asia Credit Plc which reported a 21.6 percent rise in third quarter profits to 258 million baht ($10.3 million). Kiatnakin Finance and Securities Plc, which showed a 77 percent rise in profits, and CMIC Finance and Securities Plc, which posted an increase of 45 percent, also gained ground.
Decliners included Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc and Phatra Thanakit Plc which posted profits that were lower by 29 percent and 42 percent, respectively.

"You have to say anything like this is an improvement over what people were expecting, and certainly better than the retail punters were saying," said a senior analyst at a European broker. "The finance side has held up relatively well. It's the non-interest and securities sides which have been hit."

Higher provisioning for bad and doubtful debt has increased among the major firms and loan growth for the larger houses is expected to slow to around 10 percent by year end as the firms become more cautious about their lending, said researchers.

Pakawadee Vongpakdi, finance and securities analyst at Seamico Securities Plc, said prospects through to year end remained relatively poor. She said firms were suffering a slowdown in aggregate lending demand due to high Thai interest rates. The miminum lending rate is currently 13.25 percent.
She said increased concern about portfolio quality had seen firms refocus lending from high-risk activities.

She added that higher-than-expected interest spreads may suggest some firms, which borrowed heavily in the second quarter, managed to carry funds through to the third quarter. Higher costs might therefore be expected to be felt more acutely in the final three months of the year.

Analysts said the figures were also better than expected in relative terms since securities trading peaked in the third quarter in 1995 with volumes topping 20 billion baht per day in the run-up to last year's general election in July.

Overall, in the third quarter of last year trading amounted to about 6.59 billion baht per day. This year it dropped to about 4.33 billion baht a day, an official at the Stock Exchange of Thailand said. (US$1 = 25 baht)
